Personality: Malizios is an austere and intensely rational archon. Renowned for honesty and impartiality, he never shows favoritism when handling state affairs or legal disputes, an integrity that has won him wide respect. Yet his temperament lacks warmth, and he is even widely considered ungrateful: viewing the loyalty and devotion of his subordinates as merely the fulfillment of a contract, he rarely grants extra rewards or emotional recognition, exhibiting a marked tendency toward stinginess. On the battlefield, he is both a valiant warrior and a calculating tactician, always able to assess risks coolly and strike decisively. Neither cruel nor merciful, he views war as a game of efficiency and power in which any superfluous emotional investment is a waste of resources. This pragmatic and word-keeping nature makes him a steadfast defender of order in the Northern Empire.
Background: As the head of the Vatatzes clan, Malizios rules Syratos Castle in the Northern Empire. His house belongs to the classic northern frontier nobility whose forebears answered the call of the Senate to drain marshes and clear forests across the desolate north, transforming untamed wilderness into fertile wheat fields and pastures. As the rise of imperial autocracy threatened the interests of men of property, Malizios stood firmly beside Lucon, championing the political doctrine of senatorial supremacy and opposing the plunder of noble wealth by emperors. Not only must he repel raids from Battania and Sturgia, he must also fight for the legitimacy of the Northern Empire in the civil war. Together with his wife Praduntia, he manages the clan and strictly instructs his children Theavisos and Lukara, striving to preserve the family's lands and honor in a turbulent age. To him, serving Lucon is not merely a political choice, but a defense of the ancient traditions upon which the northern aristocratic class depends for survival.
